source.note: The rules the server audit classes as client-only. Copy this list again from the audit, with its commit, whenever the audit changes; tests/test_client_only_rules.py then needs a check for every new id. R107 (browser schedules never overlap) is server-decided since PR 2184. R043 (re-send with acknowledgeProfileOnOtherOwner) is server-decided since PR 2233: a held Lead is skipped, never re-sent.

rules.rule: Use only the production Mosaico connector; never a stage, test, localhost or amplifyapp server, and never choose a server by organisation id.
rules.note: Which connector a client uses is decided on the person's machine. Mosaico names its environment on every start (next rule).

rules.rule: If no Mosaico connector is connected, stop and tell the person to connect it in Claude's connectors (not /mcp).
Never end the acting session yourself; ending it is the person's choice.
Run approved scripts only through the one-line directive; never print, retype, paraphrase, reorder, shorten or extend a script.
Never read, copy, export or reconstruct a LinkedIn cookie, token or session, and never write a LinkedIn script of your own.
rules.clientOnlyWhere: plugins/mosaico-claude/hooks/browser-script-gate.py (refuses LinkedIn and credential-store scripts); thin skill
rules.note: Matches the settled decision: LinkedIn session cookies are never exported.

rules.rule: Read each script file with the file-reading tool; if the installed plugin has no browser folder, stop and report the plugin needs updating.
Captures run in Claude's built-in browser pane only, never through the Chrome extension, and Codex cannot run them.
If LinkedIn asks for the person's email, record email-required, never cannot-message.
rules.note: Only the screen shows the email prompt; Mosaico keeps the Lead and flags it in To sort once told.

rules.rule: Record a withdrawal only after LinkedIn shows the invitation gone; never click Connect or Message in a Withdraw run.
A LinkedIn warning or captcha stops the run at once.
rules.note: Only the screen shows it; Mosaico accepts it as the proof of a blocked end (linkedInIssue).

rules.rule: Leave a record of each routine on the Routines Board in one batch; a failed board write never blocks the report.
If a tool returns contradictory state, record it with the MCP incident tool; never substitute memory for Mosaico state.
Confirm every Agent and Lead change with the person immediately before the call, and never infer a bulk target from a partial name.
Install schedules only with the three user-level browser allow rules, no stale skill copies, no active Codex automations and no non-production Mosaico server.
Schedule texts are thin: never copy a procedure step into one; a run on an older plugin stops and asks for an update; a saved Sync data task is retired, never run.
Codex reads the repair queue only and never starts a Repair run, writes or opens LinkedIn.
rules.note: Moot since 2026-10-27: the Repair queue and the Repair run are gone from the server. The Codex skill line goes with the thin plugin 0.10.0.
